name: Brand new browser profile
plain: A browser that has never been used looks empty in many small ways.
meaning: A fresh profile starts with no cookies, empty storage, a history length of one, no earlier permission choices and no extensions. A person's browser rarely looks like that. Cloud browser agents often start from a clean profile each run, so they look like first time visitors. Saving and reusing a profile between runs makes the agent look like a returning visitor.

web.api: history.length; document.cookie; localStorage.length; navigator.storage.estimate(); Notification.permission; navigator.permissions.query()

steps: Page reads history length and its own stored state
Page may read quota and permission defaults
Server notes there are no prior cookies or tokens
Combined empty state raises the score for automation

fields.name: history.length
fields.range: 1 in a new tab with no history

limits.headline: Can tell that the browser has no past
can: See an empty history and storage
Treat a first visit differently when risk is high
Reward a returning profile with fewer challenges
cannot: Tell a new person from an agent
limits.differs: New people and private windows also look fresh. Sites weigh it with other signals and give extra trust to a profile that keeps coming back.

story.what_it_is: A used browser carries traces of its owner's life. A brand new one carries none, and sites notice the blank.

marketing.name: History.length
marketing.pitch: Docs describe how many entries are in the session history of the tab.

story.for_you: You never see it. A new phone or fresh browser may get an extra check on first visit, which goes away as it is used.
story.for_makers: Do not block fresh profiles on their own. Use them as one factor, and offer a clear sign in path. If you run agents, store and reuse a profile for the same site and keep it tied to one account.

use_cases.example: A bank asks for more proof on a first visit from an empty profile.
A store applies stricter checks to a checkout from a brand new browser.
An ad verifier counts empty profiles as lower trust.
A site counts first visits using the lack of stored state.
An agent platform saves a profile so later runs look like returning visits.
A fraud team compares fresh profiles on sign up with later behavior.

risks: Penalizes new devices and private browsing

technical_bounds: Also true for new devices and private windows
Easy to fake with seeded storage
